smells.finding: Nothing in the diff is long, and the change is net-subtractive on this axis. run_facts' body is 13 lines and lost one entry; build_manifest's body is ~25 lines of one linear assembly and lost one keyword argument; the new _dirty_key_paths is 14 lines of a single recursive traversal with one job. The longest thing the diff adds is a 20-line class docstring, which is prose, not a method.

Measured rather than eyeballed: RepoRevContent, the class that absorbs almost all the test edits, is 14 methods over 149 lines, and it SHRANK by one net method (one test replaced, none added). It is mid-pack in its own file -- ManifestEnvelope is 22 methods / 219 lines and ProducerGuards is 7 / 177 -- so it is not an outlier by the file's own established scale, and all 14 methods sit on one responsibility (what repo_rev carries and what it must not).

MEASURED, not suspected. The new module-level _dirty_key_paths (tests/test_context_manifest.py:229) is the SECOND hand-rolled recursive dict/list walker over the manifest structure in the same file: assert_json_native, nested inside test_manifest_survives_the_json_round_trip at :1092, is the first, and it has the identical traversal skeleton (isinstance dict -> iterate items and recurse; isinstance list -> iterate and recurse; else terminal check). I found it by AST-scanning every function in scripts/ and tests/ for a self-recursive body mentioning both dict and list; the whole repo has exactly five such functions and two of them are these, in one file, over one data structure. They differ only in the terminal predicate -- one collects a path when the key is 'dirty', the other asserts the leaf is JSON-native. Concrete cost: a third manifest-wide property (say, no absolute paths at any depth, which the file already checks NON-recursively a few lines later) will produce a third copy. Observation, not a blocker -- the cheap fix is one walker yielding (path, value) pairs that both callers filter. Deliberately NOT overridden: I looked for a repo standard sanctioning per-test traversal helpers and none exists.

_dirty_key_paths walks the plain dict that build_manifest returns, which IS this module's published interface -- build_manifest's contract is 'returns a dict of this shape', so walking it is testing through the interface, not reaching behind it (global-everyone.md: 'The interface is the test surface'). No method in the diff is more interested in another module's data than its own: build_manifest reads exactly one key off the repo_state edge and run_facts reads only roots and its own arguments. If anything the change REDUCES envy, since build_manifest now consumes one half of the edge's return instead of routing both.

The pair {commit, dirty} travels together everywhere -- repo_revision returns it, default_repo_state returns it, the test fakes construct it inline at nine sites in RepoRevContent alone -- and is never objectified. A textbook clump, and the change makes it slightly worse in the sense that the pair is now passed whole to a consumer that wants one half.

override.repo_standard: global-everyone.md Universal posture, 'One canonical path; no speculative abstraction', read together with the ratified scope in .agent-work/issue-305/crew/g4-implement-handoff.md: 'checklist_engine.repo_revision() is out of scope and must not change: it stays a general repo-facts primitive returning {commit, dirty}.'

The standard subordinates the smell twice over: the abstraction is unwarranted on its own merits AND is out of the ruled scope. Note this override covers the CLUMP only; the separate question of whether the unused half should exist at all is flagged under speculative-generality below rather than being swept up here.

The strongest structural signal in this diff, and I have measured its cost rather than merely naming it. Removing ONE boolean from ONE dict literal required coordinated edits in five files and rewrote the same rationale -- dirty is repo-wide, it is computed before the manifest is written, so it reads its predecessor's tree -- at SEVEN prose sites: the scripts/context_manifest.py module docstring, its CONTENT_KEYS comment block, and its default_repo_state, run_facts and build_manifest docstrings; scripts/checklist_engine.py's repo_revision docstring; docs/CHECKLIST_ENGINE_DESIGN.md's narrative plus its new successor paragraph; and tests/test_context_manifest.py's RepoRevContent class docstring. This is the field's SECOND move (it went content -> run in #300 g5 rework 1, run -> gone in #327) and both moves touched the same scattered set, which is exactly the repeat-pattern evidence Fowler asks for. The cost is not hypothetical: the measurement '49 manifests, 47 true / 1 false / 1 field-absent' is now written out in TWO shipped places (scripts/context_manifest.py:34-36 and the design-doc successor paragraph) with no single source, and my c5 and d3 findings are the direct consequence -- one of those two copies carries a causal parenthetical the tree refutes, and both are stated in an unanchored present tense against a tree that has already moved to 56/51/1/4. Replicated rationale drifted, in this very commit. Deliberately NOT overridden: global-crew.md's 'match the surrounding in-file documentation conventions' sanctions matching the house style, and ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md's rules say nothing about restating a rationale N times, so no documented standard covers restating one measurement in two shipped files. Observation and triage candidate, not a blocker -- the fix is to state the measurement once, in the design doc, and have the code point at it.

scripts/context_manifest.py has exactly one axis of change here -- what the run subtree carries -- and the diff does not mix it with any second reason to change. CONTENT_KEYS, the content/run boundary, rows(), encode(), manifest_path() and write_manifest() are all untouched, which I verified mechanically (the only code objects that differ between the two revisions are run_facts and build_manifest).

No chain longer than one hop anywhere in the diff: state.get('commit'), checklist.get('work_id'), roots.get('repo'). The one multi-step expression, Path(roots[t]).as_posix(), is a conversion rather than a navigation through intermediaries, and it is untouched by this change.

The sharpest Fowler call in this diff, and it is flagged rather than overridden because the repo's OWN inherited doctrine cuts against the retention rather than sanctioning it. repo_revision/default_repo_state deliberately keep returning both halves while exactly one consumer now uses exactly one half, and the justification written into the shipped docstrings is explicitly hypothetical: 'a second caller with different needs is free to use either half.' global-everyone.md Deep-module vocabulary states the rule directly -- 'One adapter = a hypothetical seam; two = a real one -- a boundary with a single implementer is a guess until a second proves it' -- and there is one consumer, so the generality is a guess by the repo's own definition. The same section's deletion test agrees: I deleted the 'dirty': None half of default_repo_state's early return and the FULL suite stayed green (1487 passed, 2 skipped, 472 subtests, zero failures), so the unused half is not merely unused, it is unpinned. Universal posture ('no speculative abstraction') and global-crew.md ('no speculative abstraction') say the same thing. I am NOT calling this a defect of this change: the g4-implement handoff put repo_revision's behaviour out of scope and this gate correctly obeyed that, and the primitive's own contract remains fully tested at tests/test_checklist_engine.py:1075-1110. But 'a documented standard makes it acceptable' is the bar for an override, and no documented standard does -- the documented standards lean the other way -- so the honest verdict is flagged, routed to triage for whoever owns the primitive, not quietly overridden here.

The diff adds several tombstone comments -- prose describing code that is no longer there. The clearest is run_facts' docstring, which now spends seven lines on a field the function does not mention at all ('A dirty flag lived here between #300 g5 rework 1 and #327 (#305 g4), when it was removed outright ... Do not re-add it here without reading the module docstring's measurement first'), and CONTENT_KEYS' comment block, which now explains why the tuple did NOT change. Read cold, that is the classic shape of a comment compensating for something the code cannot say.

override.repo_standard: .agent-work/issue-305/crew/g4-implement-handoff.md, the ratified scope for this gate: 'The prose must record that the field was removed and why ... not merely fall silent. A reader of main must not think it was never there. Reference #327.' Reinforced by global-everyone.md Universal posture, 'Keep Constellation context and architecture docs current when their meaning changes.'
override.reason: The standard subordinates the smell because the comments are not compensating for unclear code -- the code is three deletions and reads perfectly without them -- they are carrying provenance that is genuinely unrecoverable from the code, and recording it was an explicit, ruled deliverable of this gate rather than an author's improvisation. Deodorant is a comment that exists BECAUSE the code is unclear; these exist because a reader of main would otherwise re-propose a field that has now been placed wrongly twice and measured out once. Scoped override: it covers the EXISTENCE of the tombstones, not their multiplicity -- that seven sites restate one rationale is a real cost and is flagged under shotgun-surgery above rather than being excused here.
